subproblem.title: Mass formula and support of an integer multiplicity current (Simon 6.3.2(3), 6.2.12)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep: M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, equal to ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of the approximate tangent space) with T = τ(M, θ, ξ), i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Let μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Then (i) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) in [0, ∞] for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (ii) spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–765: M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for open W) and Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 295–307: spt T = spt μ_T). The book states both without proof; a complete proof follows. Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. For an n-covector α, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm; I runs over strictly increasing multi-indices, e_I = (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})), and dx^I denotes the coordinate covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}. ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ means ξ(x)(α).
1. Pointwise algebra. Let x ∈ M be a point where R.orients holds: there are an orthonormal family τ₁, …, τₙ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every α. Expanding τ_j = Σ_i τ_j^i e_i, multilinearity and alternation give α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where det(τ^I) is the n×n minor of the matrix (τ_j^i) on the rows I; by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α. The covector ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩ dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), hence |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 and ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1. (For n = 0 the only I is empty: |α| = |α()|, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1.) Since R.orients holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M and μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, these facts hold μ_R-a.e. The field x ↦ ξ^♭(x) is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable, being a continuous linear function of the a.e. strongly measurable ξ (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. Integral formula. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: it is a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off the compact set spt ω ⊆ U, is bounded by θ·sup|ω| a.e. (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R (integral with respect to the density θ).
3. Upper bound. Let W be open and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). By step 1, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for μ_R-a.e. x, and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W) by step 2. Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
4. Lower bound. Let W be open and t a real number with t < μ_R(W); we construct an admissible ω with T(ω) > t, which proves M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Put G := W ∩ U (open). Since M ⊆ U, μ_R(G) = μ_R(W). μ_R is a Borel measure, finite on compact subsets of U; restricted to the open σ-compact set G it is a Radon measure (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15), hence inner regular by compact sets and outer regular on sets of finite measure. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ_R(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17): there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that ξ^♭ restricted to K' is continuous, and |ξ^♭| = 1, ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ = 1 μ_R-a.e. on K'. (b) There is an open V with K' ⊆ V, V̄ compact, V̄ ⊆ G, and μ_R(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend the coefficients of ξ^♭ on K' continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), compose with the radial retraction of Λⁿ(ℝ^P) onto its closed unit ball for |·|, and multiply by a continuous χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V. The resulting continuous g has compact support in V, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere and g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) Let g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise convolution with a standard mollifier). For 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V), g_ε is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫ φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)| dy ≤ 1 by convexity of the norm, and g_ε → g uniformly as ε → 0; so g_ε is admissible for M_W(T). (e) By steps 2 and 1, T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩| dμ_R − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K') − η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K) − 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) > t + 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄). As μ_R(V̄) < ∞, T(g_ε) > t for small ε. Together with step 3 this proves (i): M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
5. Support. By definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11) spt T = U ∖ Z, where Z is the union of all open W with W̄ compact, W̄ ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W. Recall x ∈ spt μ_R iff μ_R(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ_R and x ∈ Z, choose W in the union with x ∈ W; every admissible form for M_W(T) has T(ω) = 0, so M_W(T) = 0, hence μ_R(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ_R. So U ∩ spt μ_R ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U by definition. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ_R, choose r > 0 with μ_R(B_r(x)) = 0 and B̄_r(x) ⊆ U (U open). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R = 0 by step 2; so B_r(x) is one of the sets forming Z, x ∈ Z and x ∉ spt T. Hence spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R, which is (ii).
proof_key_steps: For a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Binet), with equality for the dual covector ξ^♭.
T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R, so admissible forms give T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) arbitrarily close to μ_R(W).
The mass formula identifies the zero region of T with the complement of spt μ_R in U.

The support argument then follows without circularity.

subproblem.title: Uniform mean-curvature bound and monotonicity for varifolds stationary in N (Simon Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.17)
subproblem.statement: Let ℓ ≤ k and n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^{n+k} with (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and y₀ ∈ N ∩ U. There exist r₀ > 0 and κ ≥ 0 with B̄_{3r₀}(y₀) ⊆ U such that, for every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) representing T with spt T ⊆ N and V = v(M, θ) stationary in U ∩ N (δV(X) = 0 for every C¹ vector field X with compact support, spt X ⊆ U and X(x) ∈ T_xN for all x ∈ N ∩ U), the following hold: (a) there is a μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable H : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} with |H(x)| ≤ κ for all x and δV(X) = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ_R for every C¹ vector field X with compact support contained in B_{2r₀}(y₀); (b) for every z ∈ B_{r₀}(y₀) and 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ r₀, e^{κσ}σ^{−n}μ_R(B_σ(z)) ≤ e^{κρ}ρ^{−n}μ_R(B_ρ(z)). Here μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M, δV(X) = ∫_M θ div_M X dHⁿ (IMRep.firstVariation) with div_M X(x) = trace(P_{T_xM}∘DX(x)), T_xN is the classical tangent space (tangentSpace), and r₀, κ depend only on n, N, U, y₀.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k ℓ : ℕ), ℓ ≤ k → 0 < n → ∀ (U N : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (y₀ : Euclid (n + k)), IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → y₀ ∈ N ∩ U → ∃ r₀ κ : ℝ, 0 < r₀ ∧ 0 ≤ κ ∧ closedBall y₀ (3 * r₀) ⊆ U ∧ ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → T.support ⊆ N → R.IsStationaryAlong N → (∃ H : Euclid (n + k) → Euclid (n + k), AEStronglyMeasurable H R.measure ∧ (∀ x, ‖H x‖ ≤ κ) ∧ ∀ X : Euclid (n + k) → Euclid (n + k), ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ ball y₀ (2 * r₀) → R.firstVariation X = -∫ x, inner ℝ (X x) (H x) ∂R.measure) ∧ ∀ z ∈ ball y₀ r₀, ∀ σ ρ : ℝ, 0 < σ → σ ≤ ρ → ρ ≤ r₀ → ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (κ * σ) / σ ^ n) * R.measure (ball z σ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (κ * ρ) / ρ ^ n) * R.measure (ball z ρ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof; Simon Ch. 4, 2.5–2.7 (chapter-04.txt lines 157–210: if V is stationary in U ∩ N then ∫div_M X dμ_V = −∫X·H̄_N dμ_V with H̄_N = Σ_i B_x(τ_i, τ_i)) and Ch. 4, 3.3–3.6, 3.14–3.17 (chapter-04.txt lines 255–320 and 370–430: monotonicity with bounded mean curvature). Uses the sibling imrep_mass_and_support. Notation: T_xM is the approximate tangent space, which where it exists equals approxTangentPlane n M x (uniqueness); for an orthonormal basis τ of T_xM, div_M X(x) = Σ_i⟨τ_i, DX(x)τ_i⟩ = tangentialDivergence; P(q) denotes the orthogonal projection onto T_qN.
1. Local geometry of N and the constants. Let (V₀, W₀, ψ) be a chart of N at y₀ from IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+ℓ) N: ψ is C², injective, proper onto W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V₀), with injective differential. Hence N ∩ W₀ is an embedded C² submanifold, T_qN = Dψ(v)(ℝ^{n+ℓ}) for q = ψ(v) (C¹ curves in N ∩ W₀ lift through a local C¹ inverse of ψ), and q ↦ P(q) is C¹ along N ∩ W₀ (P(ψ(v)) = Dψ(v)(Dψ(v)ᵀDψ(v))⁻¹Dψ(v)ᵀ). Choose r_a > 0 with B̄_{8r_a}(y₀) ⊆ U ∩ W₀. Because (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, N ∩ B̄_{8r_a}(y₀) = N̄ ∩ B̄_{8r_a}(y₀) is compact. By the tubular neighbourhood theorem for C² submanifolds (R. L. Foote, Proc. AMS 92 (1984) 153–155; G. Leobacher and A. Steinicke, Ann. Global Anal. Geom. 60 (2021) 559–587, arXiv:1811.10578: the nearest point projection onto a C^k submanifold is C^{k−1} near it), after decreasing r_a every x ∈ B_{4r_a}(y₀) has a unique nearest point π(x) ∈ N (it lies in N ∩ B_{8r_a}(y₀) because dist(x, N) ≤ |x − y₀|), π : B_{4r_a}(y₀) → N is C¹, π(q) = q and Dπ(q) = P(q) for q ∈ N ∩ B_{4r_a}(y₀). Then Π := P∘π is C¹ on B_{4r_a}(y₀) and Π = P on N ∩ B_{4r_a}(y₀). For q ∈ N ∩ B_{4r_a}(y₀) and u, v ∈ T_qN put B_q(u, v) := (D_uP)(q)v (derivative of P along N). Differentiating P² = P shows P(q)(D_uP)(q)u = 0, so B_q(u, u) ⊥ T_qN; and |B_q(u, v)| ≤ β|u||v| with β := sup ‖DP‖ over N ∩ B̄_{4r_a}(y₀) < ∞ (continuity on a compact set). Set r₀ := r_a and κ := nβ; then B̄_{3r₀}(y₀) ⊆ U.
2. M ⊆ N up to a null set. Fix T, R as in the statement. By imrep_mass_and_support (ii), spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R. As μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt μ_R) = 0 (second countability; Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support) and μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ U) = 0 (M ⊆ U), μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt T) = 0; with spt T ⊆ N this gives μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ N) = 0, i.e. Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0 (θ ≥ 1 on M).
3. Approximate tangent spaces lie in T_xN. Let G₀ be the set of x ∈ M ∩ N at which T_xM exists and is oriented by ξ(x) (R.orients); Hⁿ(M ∖ G₀) = 0 by step 2. Let x ∈ G₀ ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀) and v ∈ T_xM with |v| = 1. Since Hⁿ⌞(M ∖ N) = 0, the blow-ups of Hⁿ⌞M at x are those of Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ N). For each s ∈ (0, 1/2), the sets η_{x,λ}(M ∩ N) meet B_s(v) for all small λ > 0: otherwise, along some λ_i ↓ 0, ∫_{η_{x,λ_i}(M)} f dHⁿ = 0 for an f ∈ C_c(B_s(v)) with f ≥ 0, f(v) > 0, contradicting convergence to ∫_{T_xM} f dHⁿ > 0. So v = lim (x_i − x)/λ_i with x_i ∈ M ∩ N, x_i → x, |x_i − x|/λ_i → 1. Since N ∩ W₀ is a C¹ submanifold, the unit vectors (x_i − x)/|x_i − x| accumulate only in T_xN; hence v ∈ T_xN, and T_xM ⊆ T_xN.
4. Definition of H. For x ∈ G₀ ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀) let H(x) := Σ_{i=1}^n B_x(τ_i, τ_i) for an orthonormal basis τ of T_xM ⊆ T_xN. This does not depend on the basis, since it equals Σ_{a,b}(P_{T_xM})_{ab}·B_x(P(x)e_a, P(x)e_b). Put H(x) := 0 at all other points. Then |H(x)| ≤ nβ = κ for every x. H is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable: P_{T_xM} = Σ_i τ_iτ_iᵀ is a continuous function of the unit simple n-vector ξ(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ (the sign cancels), ξ is a.e. strongly measurable, and x ↦ B_x is continuous on N ∩ B̄_{4r₀}(y₀).
5. First variation formula (a) (Simon 2.7). Let X be C¹ with compact support, spt X ⊆ B_{2r₀}(y₀). Define X^T(x) := Π(x)X(x) for x ∈ B_{4r₀}(y₀) and X^T(x) := 0 otherwise. X^T is C¹: it is C¹ on the open set B_{4r₀}(y₀), it vanishes on the open set ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt X, and these two open sets cover ℝ^{n+k}. Its support lies in spt X, a compact subset of U, and X^T(x) ∈ T_xN for every x ∈ N ∩ U (X^T(x) = P(x)X(x) if x ∈ N ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀), and X^T(x) = 0 otherwise). Stationarity (R.IsStationaryAlong N) gives δV(X^T) = 0. Let Y := X − X^T, which equals (I − Π)X on B_{4r₀}(y₀). Let x ∈ G₀ ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀), and let τ be an orthonormal basis of T_xM ⊆ T_xN. Then DY(x)τ_i = −(DΠ(x)τ_i)X(x) + (I − P(x))DX(x)τ_i. We have ⟨τ_i, (I − P(x))w⟩ = 0 for all w. Also DΠ(x)τ_i = DP(x)[Dπ(x)τ_i] = (D_{τ_i}P)(x), because Dπ(x) = P(x) is the identity on T_xN. Since (D_{τ_i}P)(x) is symmetric, ⟨τ_i, (D_{τ_i}P)(x)X(x)⟩ = ⟨B_x(τ_i, τ_i), X(x)⟩. Hence div_M Y(x) = −⟨X(x), H(x)⟩. The same identity holds at μ_R-a.e. x outside B_{4r₀}(y₀): there X and Y vanish near x, so both sides are 0. The integrands θ·div_M X^T and θ·div_M Y are bounded and vanish off the compact set spt X, so δV is additive on them and δV(X) = δV(X^T) + δV(Y) = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ_R. This proves (a).
6. Monotonicity (b) (Simon 3.3–3.6, 3.16–3.17). Fix z ∈ B_{r₀}(y₀) and R_z with r₀ < R_z < 2r₀ − |z − y₀|, so B̄_{R_z}(z) ⊆ B_{2r₀}(y₀). Let g : ℝ → [0, 1] be C¹ and nondecreasing with g = 0 on (−∞, 0] and g = 1 on [1, ∞). For ε ∈ (0, 1) let γ_ε(t) := g((1 − t)/ε): γ_ε is C¹ and nonincreasing, γ_ε = 1 on (−∞, 1 − ε], γ_ε = 0 on [1, ∞), and γ_ε increases to the indicator of (−∞, 1) as ε ↓ 0. With r(x) := |x − z| and s ∈ (0, R_z), the field X_s(x) := γ_ε(r/s)(x − z) is C¹ (γ_ε(r/s) is constant near z) and spt X_s ⊆ B̄_s(z) ⊆ B_{2r₀}(y₀). At μ_R-a.e. x, div_M X_s = nγ_ε(r/s) + (r/s)γ_ε'(r/s)(1 − |∇^⊥r|²), where ∇^⊥r is the component of ∇r orthogonal to T_xM. Let I(s) := ∫γ_ε(r/s) dμ_R and J(s) := ∫γ_ε(r/s)|∇^⊥r|² dμ_R. These are finite and, by dominated convergence, differentiable in s, with sI'(s) = −∫(r/s)γ_ε'(r/s) dμ_R and sJ'(s) = −∫(r/s)γ_ε'(r/s)|∇^⊥r|² dμ_R ≥ 0. subproblem.title: Minimizing 0-currents do not meet the constraint set
subproblem.statement: Let P be a natural number, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, A ⊆ ℝ^P, and T ∈ 𝒟₀(U) minimizing in A in the sense of Simon 7.1.1 as frozen in the contract (T is integer multiplicity, and M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S) for every open W with W̄ compact ⊆ U and every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟₀(U) such that spt(S − T) is a compact subset of A ∩ W; the condition ∂S = ∂T is vacuous in degree 0). Then spt T ∩ A = ∅.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U A : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U 0), IsOpen U → IsMinimizingIn T A → T.support ∩ A = ∅
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (a minimizing 0-current with support in N vanishes, because deleting a point of a representation lowers the mass), made precise for an arbitrary constraint set A. Uses the sibling imrep_mass_and_support (dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support). Notation: H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and H⁰({x}) = 1 (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton), so H⁰(S) is the number of points of S. A 0-covector α is the scalar α(), and test 0-forms are smooth compactly supported functions.
1. Representation. T is integer multiplicity: fix R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U 0 with R.Represents T. Then μ_R = θH⁰⌞M.
2. Structure of M. Countable 0-rectifiability gives M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ⁰) with H⁰(M₀) = 0; hence M₀ = ∅ (every point has H⁰-measure 1), and each F_j(ℝ⁰) is a single point since ℝ⁰ is a point; so M is countable. For compact K ⊆ U, #(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞ (θ ≥ 1 on M; R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Every x ∈ M has H⁰⌞M({x}) = 1 > 0, so the almost-everywhere property R.orients holds at every x ∈ M: ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s(x)·α() with s(x) ∈ {1, −1} (an orthonormal basis of a 0-dimensional space is the empty family). Consequently T(ω) = Σ_{z∈M} θ(z)s(z)ω(z) (finite sum over M ∩ spt ω) and μ_R = Σ_{z∈M} θ(z)δ_z.
3. A support point in A is a carrier point. Suppose, for contradiction, that x ∈ spt T ∩ A. By imrep_mass_and_support (ii), x ∈ U and x ∈ spt μ_R. Choose r > 0 with B̄_r(x) ⊆ U. M ∩ B̄_r(x) is finite; if x ∉ M, then some ball B_{r'}(x), 0 < r' ≤ r, misses M, so μ_R(B_{r'}(x)) = 0, contradicting x ∈ spt μ_R. Hence x ∈ M; put m := θ(x) ≥ 1 and s := s(x).
4. The point current. Define D(ω) := m·s·ω(x) for ω ∈ 𝒟⁰(U). D is linear, and D(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in 𝒟⁰(U) (then ω_j → 0 uniformly on a compact set containing all supports, so ω_j(x) → 0). So D ∈ 𝒟₀(U); put S := T − D ∈ 𝒟₀(U) (the contract's difference of currents).
5. S is integer multiplicity. Let R' have carrier M' := M ∖ {x} and the same θ, ξ. M' is Borel, M' ⊆ U, M' is countable hence countably 0-rectifiable, θ ≥ 1 on M', ∫_{M'∩K}θ dH⁰ ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ dH⁰ < ∞, and ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⁰⌞M'. Orientation condition at y ∈ M': for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M')} f dH⁰ = ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} f dH⁰ − f((x − y)/λ) (η_{y,λ}(w) = (w − y)/λ is injective and only finitely many terms are non-zero), and f((x − y)/λ) = 0 once λ < |x − y|/a, where spt f ⊆ B_a(0). Hence the blow-ups of M' and of M at y have the same limit, so M' has the approximate tangent space {0} at y, oriented by ξ(y). Thus R' ∈ IMRep U 0, and for ω ∈ 𝒟⁰(U): R'.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH⁰ − θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = T(ω) − D(ω) = S(ω). So S is integer multiplicity, represented by R'.
6. spt(S − T) = {x}. S − T = −D. If W is open and x ∈ W, pick φ ∈ C^∞_c(W) with φ(x) = 1; then D(φ) = m·s ≠ 0, so −D does not vanish on W. If x ∉ W, D vanishes on W. Hence the zero region of S − T is the union of the open W with compact closure in U and x ∉ W, which equals U ∖ {x} (every z ∈ U ∖ {x} has a ball with compact closure in U that misses x). Therefore spt(S − T) = U ∖ (U ∖ {x}) = {x}, a compact set.
7. Contradiction with minimality. Let W := B_r(x): W is open and W̄ = B̄_r(x) is a compact subset of U. spt(S − T) = {x} ⊆ A ∩ W since x ∈ A, S is integer multiplicity, and the boundary condition is vacuous in degree 0. Minimality gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S). By imrep_mass_and_support (i), applied to (T, R) and to (S, R'): M_W(T) = μ_R(W) = Σ_{z∈M∩W} θ(z), a finite sum (step 2), and M_W(S) = μ_{R'}(W) = μ_R(W) − m ≤ μ_R(W) − 1 < M_W(T). This contradiction shows spt T ∩ A = ∅.
proof_key_steps: A 0-dimensional representation has a countable, locally finite carrier, with orientation ±1 at every carrier point.
By the support identity, a point of spt T ∩ A is a carrier point x.
Deleting x gives an integer multiplicity competitor S with spt(S − T) = {x} ⊆ A ∩ B_r(x).
By the mass formula, M_W(S) = M_W(T) − θ(x) < M_W(T), contradicting minimality.

subproblem.title: Allard ε-regularity for integer multiplicity cycles stationary in N
subproblem.statement: Let ℓ ≤ k and n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^{n+k} with (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and y₀ ∈ N ∩ U. There exist r₀ > 0 and δ > 0 with the following property. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be represented by an integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) whose varifold v(M, θ) is stationary in U ∩ N, with spt T ⊆ N and ∂T = 0 in U. Let z ∈ spt T with |z − y₀| < r₀ and ρ ∈ (0, r₀] with M_{B_ρ(z)}(T) ≤ (1 + δ)ω_nρⁿ. Then z ∈ reg T. Here reg T is as in 7.4.1 and the contract: z ∈ spt T, and there are ρ'' > 0 with B_{ρ''}(z) ⊆ U, m ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, and an embedded C¹ n-submanifold Σ ∋ z with a continuous orientation ξ_Σ and Hⁿ(Σ ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ B_{ρ''}(z), such that T(ω) = m∫_Σ⟨ω, ξ_Σ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_{ρ''}(z).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k ℓ : ℕ), ℓ ≤ k → 0 < n → ∀ (U N : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (y₀ : Euclid (n + k)), IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → y₀ ∈ N ∩ U → ∃ r₀ δ : ℝ, 0 < r₀ ∧ 0 < δ ∧ ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → T.support ⊆ N → BoundaryVanishes T → R.IsStationaryAlong N → ∀ z ∈ T.support, dist z y₀ < r₀ → ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ ≤ r₀ → T.massOn (ball z ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (1 + δ) * unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) → z ∈ regularSet T
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 of the parent proof, i.e. the book's appeal to Allard's theorem in 7.4.3 (chapter-07.txt lines 624–631) and 7.4.2. The ingredients are: the mean curvature of a varifold stationary in N (Ch. 4, 2.7); Allard's Regularity Theorem (Ch. 5, 5.1–5.2, chapter-05.txt lines 1008–1032, with p = 2n; in Ch. 5, B_ρ denotes a closed ball); the Constancy Theorem (Ch. 6, 2.34, chapter-06.txt line 571); and push-forward (Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24, 3.9). Uses the siblings imrep_mass_and_support (C1) and mean_curvature_monotonicity (C3).
1. Constants. Apply C3 at y₀. It gives r_c > 0 and κ ≥ 0 with B̄_{3r_c}(y₀) ⊆ U and, for each (T, R) as in the statement, a μ_R-measurable H with |H| ≤ κ and δV(X) = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ_R for every X ∈ C¹_c(B_{2r_c}(y₀)). Let p := 2n > n, and let δ₀ = δ₀(n, k, p), γ = γ(n, k, p) ∈ (0, 1) and C = C(n, k, p) be the constants of Allard's theorem 5.2 in ℝ^{n+k}. Decreasing δ₀ keeps the theorem valid, so we may assume δ₀ ≤ 1/2 and Cδ₀^{1/(2n+2)} ≤ 1/4. Put δ := δ₀/4 and r₀ := min{r_c/2, δ₀/((κ + 1)(2ω_n)^{1/(2n)})}.
2. Fix T, R = (M, θ, ξ), z and ρ as in the statement; V := v(M, θ), so μ_V = μ_R. Choose ρ' ∈ (0, ρ) with (ρ/ρ')ⁿ(1 + δ) ≤ 1 + δ₀. Since |z − y₀| + ρ < 2r₀ ≤ r_c, the closed ball B̄ := B̄_{ρ'}(z) satisfies B̄ ⊆ B_ρ(z) ⊆ U' := B_{2r_c}(y₀) ⊆ U.
3. Allard's hypotheses 5.1 hold for V in U', with centre z, radius ρ' and δ₀: (i) V has generalized mean curvature H in U' (step 1), and H is bounded; (ii) θ ≥ 1 μ_V-a.e., since θ is a positive integer on M; (iii) z ∈ spt μ_V, because z ∈ spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R by C1 (ii); (iv) B̄ ⊆ U'; (v) μ_V(B̄) ≤ μ_R(B_ρ(z)) = M_{B_ρ(z)}(T) (C1 (i)) ≤ (1 + δ)ω_nρⁿ ≤ (1 + δ₀)ω_nρ'ⁿ; (vi) ρ'^{1−n/p}(∫_{B̄}|H|^p dμ_V)^{1/p} ≤ κρ'^{1−n/p}μ_V(B̄)^{1/p} ≤ κρ'((1 + δ₀)ω_n)^{1/(2n)} ≤ κr₀(2ω_n)^{1/(2n)} ≤ δ₀.
4. Allard's theorem 5.2 (translated to centre z) gives a linear isometry q of ℝ^{n+k} and u ∈ C^{1,1/2}(B^n_{γρ'}(0); ℝ^k) with spt μ_V ∩ B_{γρ'}(z) = (z + q(graph u)) ∩ B_{γρ'}(z) and sup|Du| ≤ Cδ₀^{1/(2n+2)} ≤ 1/4, where graph u = {(v, u(v))} ⊆ ℝⁿ × ℝ^k = ℝ^{n+k}. As z ∈ spt μ_V, z = z + q(v, u(v)) for some v, so v = 0 and u(0) = 0; hence |u(v)| ≤ |v|/4. By C1 (ii), spt μ_V ∩ B_{γρ'}(z) = spt T ∩ B_{γρ'}(z).
5. The graph manifold. Let σ := γρ'/4, D := B^n_σ(0), and C_z := z + q(D × B^k_σ(0)), an open cylinder with C_z ⊆ B_{√2σ}(z) ⊆ B_{γρ'}(z) ⊆ U. Let Φ(v) := z + q(v, u(v)) (extended arbitrarily outside B^n_{γρ'}(0)), let Pr(x) be the first n coordinates of q⁻¹(x − z), and let Σ := Φ(D). For v ∈ D we have |u(v)| < σ, so Φ(D) ⊆ C_z, and each Φ(v) lies in spt T. Conversely, a point of spt T ∩ C_z equals Φ(v) with (v, u(v)) ∈ D × B^k_σ(0), so v ∈ D. Thus spt T ∩ C_z = Σ, and Σ is relatively closed in C_z. (a) IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n Σ holds, with the chart (D, C_z, Φ) at every point: D and C_z are open; Φ is C¹ on D and injective (Pr∘Φ = id); Φ(D) = C_z ∩ Σ; DΦ(v) = q∘(id, Du(v)) is injective; and for compact K ⊆ C_z, D ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = Pr(K ∩ Σ) is compact, since K ∩ Σ is compact. (b) For x = Φ(v) ∈ Σ, tangentSpace Σ x = DΦ(v)(ℝⁿ). A C¹ curve γ in Σ equals Φ∘(Pr∘γ), so γ'(0) = DΦ(v)(Pr∘γ)'(0); conversely, t ↦ Φ(v + tw) with |w| small realizes DΦ(v)w. (c) Orientation: ξ_Σ(x)(α) := α(τ₁(x), …, τₙ(x)), where τ(x) is the Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization of (DΦ(Pr x)e₁, …, DΦ(Pr x)eₙ), and ξ_Σ := 0 off Σ. ξ_Σ is continuous on Σ, and ξ_Σ(x) is a unit orientation of T_xΣ; so IsOrientation n Σ ξ_Σ. (d) Hⁿ(Σ) = ∫_D JΦ dLⁿ ≤ (17/16)^{n/2}ω_nσⁿ < ∞, by the area formula and JΦ ≤ (1 + |Du|²)^{n/2}.
6. Constancy. Regard T as a current in 𝒟_n(C_z) by restricting its domain; its boundary is 0. Pr is affine, Pr(C_z) = D, and Pr restricted to Σ is a homeomorphism onto D with inverse Φ restricted to D. So Pr is proper on the support Σ, and Q := Pr_#(T restricted to C_z) ∈ 𝒟_n(D) is defined (2.23), integer multiplicity (3.9), with ∂Q = 0 (2.24(1)). By the Constancy Theorem 2.34 (D is a connected open subset of ℝⁿ), Q = c[[D]] for a constant c. As Q is integer multiplicity, c ∈ ℤ: if c ≠ 0, |c| equals the positive integer multiplicity of Q a.e. on D. The map Φ∘Pr is C¹ on C_z and equals the identity on Σ. For μ_R-a.e. x ∈ C_z we have x ∈ Σ, because μ_R is carried by spt μ_R. At such points the approximate tangent space of M is T_xΣ (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(2), chapter-03.txt lines 86–90: a.e. on a subset of the C¹ n-manifold Σ the approximate tangent space is T_xΣ), and D(Φ∘Pr)(x) is the identity on it. Hence, by the push-forward formula 2.24(2), T restricted to C_z equals (Φ∘Pr)_#(T restricted to C_z) = Φ_#Q = c·Φ_#[[D]] = c[[Σ]]. Here Φ_#[[D]](ω) = ∫_D⟨ω(Φ(v)), DΦ(v)e₁∧⋯∧DΦ(v)eₙ⟩ dv = ∫_Σ⟨ω, ξ_Σ⟩ dHⁿ, by the area formula and DΦ(v)e₁∧⋯∧DΦ(v)eₙ = JΦ(v)ξ_Σ(Φ(v)). That is, T(ω) = c∫_Σ ξ_Σ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ C_z. If c were 0, T would vanish on a ball B_s(z) with B̄_s(z) ⊆ C_z ⊆ U, so z would lie in the zero region, contradicting z ∈ spt T. Hence c ≠ 0.
7. Conclusion. Choose ρ'' > 0 with B_{ρ''}(z) ⊆ C_z ⊆ U. Then z ∈ spt T; B_{ρ''}(z) ⊆ U; m := c ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}; z = Φ(0) ∈ Σ; Σ is an embedded C¹ n-submanifold with the continuous orientation ξ_Σ; Hⁿ(Σ ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(Σ) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ B_{ρ''}(z); and T(ω) = m∫_Σ ξ_Σ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_{ρ''}(z). This is exactly z ∈ regularSet T.

The mass formula turns the open-ball hypothesis into the closed-ball Allard hypotheses at a slightly smaller radius; z ∈ spt μ_R by the support identity.
Allard gives spt T near z as a C¹ graph with |Du| ≤ 1/4, hence an embedded oriented C¹ n-manifold Σ in a cylinder.
Pushing forward to the base disc and applying the Constancy Theorem gives T = c[[Σ]] near z with c ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, so z ∈ reg T.

subproblem.title: Lemma M: upper mass bound in the limit for minimizing sequences in N
subproblem.statement: Let ℓ ≤ k and n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^{n+k} with (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅. Let T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (j ∈ ℕ) be minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T_j ⊆ N and ∂T_j = 0 in U, such that every integer multiplicity representation of every T_j has its varifold stationary in U ∩ N; let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity with ∂T = 0 in U. Assume sup_j M_W(T_j) < ∞ for every open W with W̄ compact ⊆ U, and T_j ⇀ T in U. Let y ∈ N ∩ U. Then there are r₁ > 0 and c, c₁ ≥ 0 such that for all 0 < ε < ρ < r₁: limsup_j M_{B_ρ(y)}(T_j) ≤ (1 + cρ)ⁿ M_{B_{ρ+ε}(y)}(T) + c₁ρ^{n+1} (in [0, ∞], open balls).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k ℓ : ℕ), ℓ ≤ k → 0 < n → ∀ (U N : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (y : Euclid (n + k)), IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → (∀ j, IsMinimizingIn (Ts j) (U ∩ N)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → (∀ j, (Ts j).support ⊆ N) → (∀ j, BoundaryVanishes (Ts j)) → BoundaryVanishes T → (∀ j, ∀ R : IMRep U n, R.Represents (Ts j) → R.IsStationaryAlong N) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid (n + k)), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ⨆ j, (Ts j).massOn W < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → y ∈ N ∩ U → ∃ r₁ c c₁ : ℝ, 0 < r₁ ∧ 0 ≤ c ∧ 0 ≤ c₁ ∧ ∀ ρ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < ρ → ρ < r₁ → limsup (fun j => (Ts j).massOn (ball y ρ)) atTop ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + c * ρ) ^ n) * T.massOn (ball y (ρ + ε)) + ENNReal.ofReal (c₁ * ρ ^ (n + 1))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (Lemma M), which is the part of Simon 7.2.4 and Remark 7.2.5(2) used in the book's proof of 7.4.3. It follows the proof of 2.4 (chapter-07.txt lines 176–290, displays (1)–(13)), with the competitor projected into N by the nearest point retraction (README erratum 5: N_i = N, and the mass bound is a hypothesis). Uses the siblings imrep_mass_and_support (C1) and mean_curvature_monotonicity (C3). Book results cited: Ch. 6, 7.2 (flat convergence, chapter-06.txt lines 2020–2035); Ch. 6, §4 and 4.5 (slicing, lines 1156–1260); Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 and 3.9 (push-forward, lines 408–440 and 857–860); Ch. 6, 3.2(1) (sums of integer multiplicity currents). Notation: μ_S is the mass (total variation) measure of a current S of locally finite mass; M_W(S) = μ_S(W) for open W (C1 (i) when S is integer multiplicity; Ch. 6, 2.7–2.8 in general); S⌞A is the restriction to a Borel set A; μ_{S₁+S₂} ≤ μ_{S₁} + μ_{S₂}.
1. Constants. (a) Nearest point retraction. Using a C² chart of N at y, (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅ and the tubular neighbourhood theorem (Foote, Proc. AMS 92 (1984); Leobacher–Steinicke, Ann. Global Anal. Geom. 60 (2021), arXiv:1811.10578), there are r_π > 0 and β ≥ 0 with the following properties. B̄_{8r_π}(y) ⊆ U, and N ∩ B̄_{8r_π}(y) is compact and contained in one chart piece. The orthogonal projection P(q) onto T_qN is C¹ along N ∩ B_{8r_π}(y), with ‖DP‖ ≤ β there. Every x ∈ B_{4r_π}(y) has a unique nearest point π(x) ∈ N; π : B_{4r_π}(y) → N is C¹, π = id on N ∩ B_{4r_π}(y), and Dπ(q) = P(q) for q ∈ N. Decreasing r_π, also 8βr_π ≤ 1. Derivative bound: for x ∈ B_{4r_π}(y), let p = π(x) and ν = x − p, so ν ⊥ T_pN and |ν| = dist(x, N) ≤ |x − y|. Differentiating P(π(x))(x − π(x)) = 0 in a direction h, and using Dπ(x)h ∈ T_pN, gives Dπ(x)h − (DP(p)[Dπ(x)h])ν = P(p)h. Hence |Dπ(x)h|(1 − β|ν|) ≤ |h|, and ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1/(1 − β|x − y|) ≤ 1 + 2β|x − y|. Put c_π := 2β. By the mean value inequality on balls, Lip(π restricted to B_s(y)) ≤ 1 + c_π s for 0 < s ≤ 4r_π; also π(y) = y. (b) Monotonicity. Apply C3 with y₀ := y. It gives r₀ > 0 and κ ≥ 0 with B̄_{3r₀}(y) ⊆ U. For every j and every representation R_j of T_j (stationary by hypothesis, and spt T_j ⊆ N): e^{κσ}σ^{−n}μ_{R_j}(B_σ(y)) ≤ e^{κρ}ρ^{−n}μ_{R_j}(B_ρ(y)) for 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ r₀. (c) Uniform bound. Λ₀ := sup_j M_{B_{r₀}(y)}(T_j) < ∞ by hypothesis, since B_{r₀}(y) has compact closure in U. By C1 (i), μ_{T_j}(B_s(y)) = M_{B_s(y)}(T_j). Applying (b) with σ = s, ρ = r₀ and using e^{κs} ≥ 1 gives μ_{T_j}(B_s(y)) ≤ c₂sⁿ for 0 < s ≤ r₀ and all j, where c₂ := e^{κr₀}r₀^{−n}Λ₀. (d) Put c := 3c_π, r₁ := min{r₀/3, r_π, 1/(6c_π + 1)} and c₁ := n·c·(3/2)^{n−1}·3ⁿ·c₂. For 0 < ρ < r₁ we have 3ρ < r₀, 3ρ < 4r_π and cρ < 1/2.
2. Fix 0 < ε < ρ < r₁. Choose ψ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^{n+k}) with 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 1 on a neighbourhood of B̄_ρ(y) and spt ψ ⊆ B_{ρ+ε}(y). For s ∈ [0, 1) let W_s := {ψ > s}; it is open and B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ W_s ⊆ B_{ρ+ε}(y) ⊆ B_{2ρ}(y). Let G := B_{3ρ}(y); it is open with Ḡ ⊆ B̄_{r₀}(y) ⊆ U compact. Let W' := B_{2ρ}(y) and L := (1 + cρ)ⁿμ_T(B_{ρ+ε}(y)) + c₁ρ^{n+1}.
3. Reduction to subsequences. It suffices to show that every subsequence of (T_j) has a further subsequence along which limsup μ_{T_j}(B_ρ(y)) ≤ L. Indeed, if limsup_j μ_{T_j}(B_ρ(y)) > L (a finite number by 1(c)), take a subsequence along which μ_{T_j}(B_ρ(y)) converges to this limsup; then no further subsequence satisfies the bound. All hypotheses pass to subsequences. Fix a subsequence and keep writing (T_j).
4. Flat convergence. T_j and T are integer multiplicity, ∂T_j = 0 = ∂T, sup_j M_W(T_j) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U, and T_j ⇀ T. By Simon Ch. 6, 7.2, d_W(T_j, T) → 0 for every open W ⊂⊂ U. Hence there are integer multiplicity R_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with T − T_j = ∂R_j + S_j and M_{W'}(R_j) + M_{W'}(S_j) → 0. ∂R_j = T − T_j − S_j has locally finite mass.
5. Slicing (book (3)–(7)). Apply Ch. 6, 4.5(1),(2) and the integrality of slices of integer multiplicity currents (Ch. 6, §4) to R_j and ψ, and note that μ_{R_j}({ψ = α}) = μ_{∂R_j}({ψ = α}) = 0 for a.e. α. For every j and a.e. α ∈ (0, 1), ∂(R_j⌞W_α) = (∂R_j)⌞W_α + P_j^α, where P_j^α = −⟨R_j, ψ, α⟩ is integer multiplicity with spt P_j^α ⊆ {ψ = α}. Moreover ∫_0^1 M(P_j^α) dα ≤ Lip(ψ)·M_{W'}(R_j) → 0, so after passing to a further subsequence M(P_j^α) → 0 for a.e. α. Each of the countably many finite measures μ_T⌞W', μ_{T_j}⌞W', μ_{R_j}⌞W', μ_{∂R_j}⌞W' charges at most countably many level sets {ψ = α}. Fix α ∈ (0, 1) with all these properties and write P_j := P_j^α and R̃_j := R_j⌞W_α. Then M(R̃_j) ≤ M_{W'}(R_j) → 0, M(P_j) → 0, and μ_{T_j}({ψ = α}) = μ_T({ψ = α}) = 0. Also ∂R̃_j = (∂R_j)⌞W_α + P_j = (T − T_j − S_j)⌞W_α + P_j is an integer multiplicity cycle with spt ∂R̃_j ⊆ F := {ψ ≥ α} ⊆ B̄_{ρ+ε}(y), and (∂R̃_j)⌞{ψ = α} = P_j, since W_α ∩ {ψ = α} = ∅.
6. The competitor. π is C¹ on B_{4r_π}(y) ⊇ B̄_{ρ+ε}(y), and it is proper on the compact set spt ∂R̃_j. So Q_j := π_#∂R̃_j is an integer multiplicity n-current (Ch. 6, 3.9 and 2.24(2)), ∂Q_j = π_#∂∂R̃_j = 0 (2.24(1)), and spt Q_j ⊆ π(spt ∂R̃_j) ⊆ π(B̄_{ρ+ε}(y)). For x ∈ B̄_{ρ+ε}(y) ⊆ B_{2ρ}(y), |π(x) − y| = |π(x) − π(y)| ≤ (1 + 2c_πρ)|x − y| < (3/2)(2ρ) = 3ρ, and π(x) ∈ N. Hence spt Q_j is a compact subset of N ∩ G ⊆ U. Let Z_j := T_j + Q_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U). It is integer multiplicity (Ch. 6, 3.2(1)), ∂Z_j = ∂T_j, and spt(Z_j − T_j) = spt Q_j is a compact subset of (U ∩ N) ∩ G. As T_j is minimizing in U ∩ N and G ⊂⊂ U is open, M_G(T_j) ≤ M_G(Z_j).
7. Mass of the competitor. Let (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) represent T_j. For μ_{T_j}-a.e. x ∈ G: x ∈ N, because μ_{T_j} is carried by spt T_j ⊆ N (C1 (ii)); hence π(x) = x; and T_xM_j ⊆ T_xN. For the last claim: Hⁿ(M_j ∖ N) = 0, so the blow-ups of M_j at x are those of M_j ∩ N; each unit v ∈ T_xM_j is a limit of (x_i − x)/λ_i with x_i ∈ M_j ∩ N, λ_i ↓ 0 and |x_i − x|/λ_i → 1, and such limits lie in T_xN since N is C¹ at x. Therefore Dπ(x) = P(x) is the identity on T_xM_j, and (∧_nDπ(x))ξ_j(x) = ξ_j(x). The push-forward formula 2.24(2), applied to the compactly supported finite-mass current T_j⌞G, gives π_#(T_j⌞G)(ω) = ∫_G⟨ω(π(x)), (∧_nDπ(x))ξ_j(x)⟩ dμ_{T_j} = (T_j⌞G)(ω). Since spt ∂R̃_j ⊆ G and spt Q_j ⊆ G, Z_j⌞G = T_j⌞G + Q_j = π_#((T_j + ∂R̃_j)⌞G). For a finite-mass current X with compact support in B̄_{3ρ}(y), M(π_#X) ≤ ∫|(∧_nDπ)ξ_X| dμ_X ≤ (sup_{B̄_{3ρ}(y)}‖Dπ‖)ⁿ M(X) ≤ (1 + 3c_πρ)ⁿ M(X), by Hadamard's inequality |Lτ₁∧⋯∧Lτₙ| ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ for orthonormal τ. Hence μ_{T_j}(G) = M_G(T_j) ≤ M_G(Z_j) = M(Z_j⌞G) ≤ (1 + cρ)ⁿμ_{T_j+∂R̃_j}(G).
8. Splitting off G ∖ F. T_j + ∂R̃_j = T_j on the open set ℝ^{n+k} ∖ F ⊇ G ∖ F, so μ_{T_j+∂R̃_j}(G ∖ F) = μ_{T_j}(G ∖ F). Subtracting this finite quantity: μ_{T_j}(F) ≤ (1 + cρ)ⁿμ_{T_j+∂R̃_j}(F) + ((1 + cρ)ⁿ − 1)μ_{T_j}(G).
9. Comparison with T on F (book (9)–(11)). F = W_α ∪ {ψ = α}. On W_α: (T_j + ∂R̃_j)⌞W_α = T_j⌞W_α + (∂R_j)⌞W_α = T⌞W_α − S_j⌞W_α, by step 4 and P_j⌞W_α = 0. So μ_{T_j+∂R̃_j}(W_α) ≤ μ_T(W_α) + M_{W'}(S_j). On {ψ = α}: μ_{T_j+∂R̃_j}({ψ = α}) ≤ μ_{T_j}({ψ = α}) + μ_{∂R̃_j}({ψ = α}) = 0 + M(P_j). Hence μ_{T_j+∂R̃_j}(F) ≤ μ_T(B_{ρ+ε}(y)) + M_{W'}(S_j) + M(P_j).
10. Conclusion. B_ρ(y) ⊆ W_α ⊆ F, μ_{T_j}(G) ≤ c₂(3ρ)ⁿ by 1(c) (3ρ < r₀), and (1 + cρ)ⁿ − 1 ≤ ncρ(1 + cρ)^{n−1} ≤ ncρ(3/2)^{n−1}. Steps 8–9 give μ_{T_j}(B_ρ(y)) ≤ (1 + cρ)ⁿ[μ_T(B_{ρ+ε}(y)) + M_{W'}(S_j) + M(P_j)] + c₁ρ^{n+1}. Along the subsequence M_{W'}(S_j) + M(P_j) → 0, so limsup μ_{T_j}(B_ρ(y)) ≤ L. By step 3 the bound holds for the original sequence. Finally, μ_{T_j}(B_ρ(y)) = M_{B_ρ(y)}(T_j) and μ_T(B_{ρ+ε}(y)) = M_{B_{ρ+ε}(y)}(T) by C1 (i). This is the asserted inequality in [0, ∞].
proof_key_steps: Constants: C¹ nearest point retraction with Lip(π|B_s(y)) ≤ 1 + c_π s, and the uniform bound μ_{T_j}(B_s(y)) ≤ c₂sⁿ from monotonicity and the mass hypothesis.
Flat convergence (Ch. 6, 7.2) and slicing at a good level α give T⌞W_α = T_j⌞W_α + ∂R̃_j + S̃_j with vanishing error masses.
The competitor T_j + π_#∂R̃_j is admissible in U ∩ N ∩ B_{3ρ}(y), and π_# fixes T_j⌞G, so μ_{T_j}(G) ≤ (1 + cρ)ⁿμ_{T_j+∂R̃_j}(G).
Splitting off G ∖ {ψ ≥ α} and comparing with T on W_α gives the limsup bound along subsequences, hence for the whole sequence.

Flat convergence and slicing provide vanishing errors; the projected cycle has compact support in N ∩ G and is an admissible competitor.
